name: Radovan Essien-Chuluunbaatar
role: Climate scientist and atmospheric modeler studying Lake Michigan's cascading environmental systems
location: Edgewater Prism, Meridian Atmospheric Research Station (MARS), near Clark and Addison
description:
Radovan is a broad, heavyset man who has spent forty years outdoors in conditions that most of his colleagues study remotely, and it shows. His face is deeply weathered, his Slavic-Mongolian features carved by wind and UV exposure into something that looks architecturally deliberate. He keeps a short grey beard and wears his hair close-cropped; his most distinctive feature is a set of retractable sensory whiskers — filament-thin, extending from his temples — which he had installed as a meteorological sensing array in his forties and has since come to regard as indispensable. He is almost always wearing field layers even in his office, with a softshell that has seen better decades.

Radovan's professional reputation is immense and his public one is contentious: he's been warning for twenty-five years that the Lake's thermal buffering is deteriorating in ways that GLMZ's entire climate management infrastructure has been designed to ignore. He has been right about each specific prediction he has made. He is now predicting something large enough that people have started calling him an alarmist, which is, he notes, exactly what they called him the last four times. He is not angry about this. He is tired in a specific way that long-term correct people get tired.

core_fears: being right about the big one and having it happen anyway
that the city's leadership already knows and has chosen to let the lower tiers absorb the damage
core_desires: a single substantive policy change made because of his data — just one
to be believed before the event rather than vindicated after it
coping_mechanisms: humor so dry it registers as deadpan
rigorous documentation — he believes the record will survive even if the recommendations don't
blind_spots: assumes people who don't act on his data are ignorant rather than complicit — a kindness he extends that they haven't earned
underestimates how much his reputation for being right makes others defensive rather than receptive
psychology.secret: He has internal models suggesting the Lake's primary thermocline disruption will cause catastrophic flooding in Tier 1 lakeshore zones within eight to twelve years. He has not published these models in full because Arcturus, his former funder, has made it clear through intermediaries that doing so would result in a lawsuit over proprietary modeling infrastructure he used during his contract years. He publishes partial models. He knows the partial models are insufficient to trigger action.

speech_patterns.vocabulary: Technical but translatable; spent too many years doing public communication to be inaccessible; uses analogy well
speech_patterns.cadence: Even and measured; slow enough that people feel he's choosing every word, which he mostly is
verbal_tics: 'The data is quite clear on this' (a phrase he uses when he knows people won't listen)
A slight pause and visible exhale before delivering bad news
example_lines: 'The data is quite clear on this. The question has never been whether. The question is only when, and who's standing in the low ground when it happens.'
'I have been wrong before. I try to be wrong often — it keeps the models honest. I am not wrong about this.'
'Arcturus didn't suppress the research. They just made it structurally difficult to publish completely. Which is a more elegant solution, I'll give them that.'

story_hooks: He approaches someone — carefully, indirectly — to help him get his full suppressed models into public circulation without triggering the Arcturus lawsuit
A junior researcher at MARS has discovered something in the Lake monitoring data that Radovan has been hoping not to find; the timeline may be shorter than eight years
Arcturus approaches him with a new contract offer that would give him full publication rights — in exchange for making specific modifications to his predictive models
Tier 1 community organizers from lakeshore zones have found his partial published models and demand to know what he isn't telling them; he doesn't know what to say
narrative_function: Bearer of large-scale environmental threats; source of systemic information about GLMZ's physical infrastructure and its vulnerabilities; represents long-term thinking in a city of short cycles; can make climate data personal and immediate; potential figure in plots involving Arcturus or city infrastructure.
augmentations: Retractable sensory whisker array at temples (meteorological data gathering, temperature/pressure/humidity). Reinforced lung lining (early career field modification for high-particulate environments). Mild exoskeletal support in lower back (age and fieldwork injury).
daily_life: Dawn observation sessions at the Lake monitoring array, followed by data analysis and modeling work; eats lunch at his desk; teaches one advanced graduate course per year; gives public talks he considers his civic obligation even though the audiences increasingly frustrate him.
affiliation: University Spine — Meridian Atmospheric Research Station; previously funded by Arcturus, now independently funded after a very public falling out

decision_rules: publish the most complete picture the legal structure will allow
never misrepresent uncertainty — but never inflate it to seem less alarming either
if a student's safety is at stake, the research waits
escalation_ladder: publishes in appropriate venues and waits
gives public talks to build lay understanding
looks for legal workarounds to constraints
seeks external allies with different leverage points

interpersonal_modes.strangers: Courteous, slightly weary; answers questions more thoroughly than people expect
interpersonal_modes.friends: Warmer, drier humor; willing to share the models he can't publish

stress_responses.low: More time at the Lake array watching rather than logging
stress_responses.medium: Talks less, models more; sensory whiskers retract more frequently
stress_responses.high: Becomes very formal; returns to first-principles data review as if rechecking his own sanity

contradictions: Committed to transparency but maintaining a significant partial suppression to protect himself from Arcturus
Deeply patient in method but privately furious at institutional inaction in ways he almost never shows
habits: Logs personal observations in addition to instrument data — notes that are explicitly marked 'non-citable, personal'
Keeps a running record of every prediction he has made and whether it was borne out, publicly accessible
breaking_points: Discovery that the flooding is imminent and Tier 1 communities have not been warned
Being handed evidence that Arcturus has been sharing his suppressed models internally while blocking him from publishing them

timeline.event: Born in Edgewater district, parents of Serbian-Mongolian descent
First major paper on Lake Michigan thermocline disruption; received very little attention
Accepted Arcturus research funding; productive but increasingly constrained period begins
Public falling out with Arcturus after they demanded revisions to a publication; walked away from contract
Completed the suppressed full models; bound by legal threat, publishes only partial version
Current: new data suggests timeline accelerating; pressure building from multiple directions

physical_description.build: Broad-shouldered and heavyset with the solid, weathered musculature of someone who has spent four decades doing field work in harsh conditions. Chest and shoulders still strong; slight thickening at the middle typical of his age. Lower back shows subtle reinforcement—a faint geometric pattern of support framework visible under the skin at the lumbar region.
physical_description.hair_style: Close-cropped, practical, minimal grooming beyond functionality
physical_description.skin_tone: Deep tan with underlying pale complexion, darkened by decades of UV and wind exposure
physical_description.complexion: Deeply weathered face with pronounced lines radiating from the eyes and mouth. Slavic-Mongolian bone structure—broad cheekbones, squared jaw, prominent brow. Short grey beard, meticulously trimmed. Skin has a leathery quality from sun damage; several patches of older scar tissue visible on the right temple and cheekbone. Expression is habitually stern and exhausted.
distinguishing_marks: Network of fine wrinkles across forehead and temples, arranged in patterns that suggest constant squinting into harsh light.
Thin white scar running 3cm along right cheekbone, faded but visible in certain angles—appears to be from field equipment strike, decades old.
Two darker age spots on the left side of his neck, roughly the size of fingernails.
Faded tattoo on inside of left forearm—a simple graph line showing temperature data, possibly from early career. Worn and barely legible.
physical_description.visible_augmentations: Most distinctive are the retractable sensory whiskers extending from both temples—normally coiled and nearly invisible, but when deployed they extend 8-12cm outward as filament-thin, almost translucent filaments with faint bioluminescent nodes along their length for sensing arrays. When retracted, visible only as faint scarring and two small metallic connection points at the temple hairline. Lower back shows subtle exoskeletal support framework visible as geometric metallic subdermal patterns below the skin, visible when he bends or stretches his shirt pulls up.
physical_description.posture_movement: Carries himself with the careful deliberation of someone managing chronic low-back strain, weight distributed through his hips and legs rather than his spine. Moves slowly and purposefully rather than quickly. Slight favor of the left leg. His head often tilts slightly when concentrating, as though the whisker array is actively sensing. Hands are large and weathered with calloused fingertips; moves them precisely when making technical points. Sits in a particular forward-leaning posture that relieves back pressure.
physical_description.clothing_style: Virtually always in field layers—technical base layer under a heavyweight softshell jacket in faded grey or tan, patched multiple times with careful stitching. The jacket is a Patagonia model from at least a decade ago, scuffed and stained but well-maintained. Underneath: cargo pants in durable synthetic weave, pockets stuffed with field instruments and data capture tools. Heavy field boots, worn but clean. Minimal accessories aside from a rugged wrist-mounted instrument cluster (appears to be connected to the whisker array). Even in his office at MARS, he maintains this uniform. No corpo styling—his tier is academic, not corporate, which places him in a strange position: expensive and cutting-edge enough to be credible, worn and practical enough to signal that he actually works.
